cards.title: Second viola handoff
cards.reason: The red-polo part (e) sustains through roughly 53.4 s, then has a long gap before its next clear attack around 57.4 s. During that interval c carries a moving mid-register phrase beginning near 53.9 s; the local candidates show successive changing pitches rather than a single held overlap. The target is the continuing pale-shirt viola (slot 2), muted so the player can take that line.

cards.title: Printed-shirt violin returns
cards.reason: In the second half, a is quiet through the shared lull after about 72 s and resumes at 74.54 s. Four perceptual attacks are estimated near 74.54, 75.12, 75.52 and 76.01 s; the fourth release is placed near 76.43 s. The rising short sequence and visible bowing in the printed-shirt violin panel support this return. Stem pitch-run segmentation can split one note or merge repeated notes, so the four-note boundary is approximate.

cards.title: Staggered violin re-entry
cards.reason: The first later passage with a shared violin quiet window is around 72.2–74.5 s: a's first return is estimated at 74.54, while d waits until about 75.84, over a second later. The loop ends after d's third new attack, near 76.73 s. a is the earlier violin and is intentionally removed; the remaining requested balance is cello b .8, pale-shirt viola c .7, red-polo viola e .3 and later violin d .5. Brief residual energy and uncertain note segmentation make the exact silent-window boundary less certain than the stagger.
